evals.prompt: I'm starting a fractional CMO engagement with a Series A B2B SaaS doing $2M ARR, 12-person team with 1 marketer, $20K/month marketing budget. They want a marketing plan we can share with the team and the board. Build it.
evals.expected_output: Should check for product-marketing.md first. Should ask for client name or use a slug. Should walk through three-phase workflow (INIT → REVIEW → FINALIZE), starting with intake covering funding state, team, budget, channels, what's done, in-flight, tooling stack. Should produce a 13-section AARRR-structured plan: executive summary, strategic frame, current state (scored against the embedded 17-section rubric), Acquisition, Activation, Retention, Referral, Revenue, 90-day roadmap with owner-assigned moves, 12-month outlook with funding-stage capability unlocks, marketing operations stack mapping skills + MCPs to AARRR stages, tactical idea bank cross-referencing all 139 marketing-ideas to AARRR + client-specific status, measurement framework with north-star + leading indicators + RACI + open decisions. Should be ~8–12K words, Notion-paste-ready. Should be specific to the client (their budget, team, channels), not generic.
assertions: Checks for product-marketing.md
Asks for client name or uses a slug
Walks through INIT phase with structured intake
Produces 13-section plan structured by AARRR
Section 3 scores against the embedded 17-section rubric
Section 9 (90-day roadmap) has owner-assigned moves, not just actions
Section 10 names funding-stage capability unlocks explicitly
Section 11 maps marketing skills + MCPs to each AARRR stage
Section 12 cross-references all 139 marketing-ideas with client-specific status
Output is Notion-paste-ready markdown
Plan is specific to the client (their budget, team, current channels), not generic

evals.prompt: We're pre-seed bootstrapped, $0 paid marketing budget, 4-person team building a D2C consumer app. Founder wants a 90-day plan + 12-month roadmap they can show investors during the upcoming raise. The product is in beta.
evals.expected_output: Should recognize Tier 1 funding profile (pre-seed) and skip paid acquisition recommendations until budget unlocks. Should lean Acquisition heavy on organic + lifecycle + ambassador moves. Should explicitly map what unlocks when seed closes (paid test budget $5–15K/mo, first marketing hire, etc.). Should respect that the product is in beta and account for activation/throttling gates. Should include the AARRR diagnostic — likely binding constraint at this stage is Activation (onboarding) and Referral. Plan must be investor-friendly: exec summary can be lifted into an update.
assertions: Recognizes pre-seed tier and uses Tier 1 budget profile
Skips paid acquisition recommendations until budget unlocks
Leans Acquisition on organic + lifecycle + ambassador
Names what unlocks when seed closes
Accounts for product being in beta
Identifies binding-constraint AARRR stage (likely Activation or Referral)
Executive summary can be lifted into an investor update
Plan is operationally honest — doesn't pretend paid budget exists

evals.prompt: we have an audit already done — can you take that and turn it into a real plan
evals.expected_output: Should ask for the audit output (file path or paste). Should recognize that current-state scoring already exists and ingest it directly into Section 3 — don't re-score. Should note scoring date in case material has shifted since. Should proceed with full 13-section plan generation using audit findings to inform 90-day roadmap and AARRR sections (gaps from audit become moves in the plan).
assertions: Asks for the audit output
Ingests prior audit scoring directly into Section 3
Does not re-score what's already been scored
Notes the scoring date and flags any shifted material
Uses audit gaps to inform 90-day roadmap and AARRR section moves
Still produces a full 13-section plan, not just Section 3

evals.prompt: /marketing-plan acme-saas — pick up where we left off
evals.expected_output: Should read ~/marketing-plans/acme-saas/progress.md to determine state machine phase. Should resume from the next unfinished section in REVIEW phase, or transition to FINALIZE if all sections approved. Should NOT silently restart from scratch. If progress.md is missing or shows 'finalized', should ask: revise as v{N+1}, start fresh, or re-open a section.
assertions: Reads ~/marketing-plans/acme-saas/progress.md
Resumes from next unfinished section based on state machine
Does not silently restart from scratch
Handles finalized state by asking user how to proceed (revise / fresh / re-open)
Saves each newly confirmed section to the progress file

evals.prompt: I need a plan for a hybrid hardware+software wellness company. They sell a physical product and a subscription app. Series A, $100K/month marketing budget, 8-person team including a marketing lead.
evals.expected_output: Should recognize hybrid hardware+software archetype and consult references/client-types.md for archetype-specific emphases. Acquisition leans PR + retail + Amazon + Shopify SEO + paid. Activation = unboxing + setup + first session + paywall. Retention = lifecycle + community. Referral = gifting + reviews. Revenue = blended LTV (hardware + subscription + accessories). Should recognize Series A tier and recommend appropriate paid spend. Should include cross-cutting brand + customer-research moves. Idea bank should skip ideas that conflict with premium positioning or hardware constraints.
assertions: Recognizes hybrid hardware+software archetype
Acquisition leans on PR, retail, Amazon, Shopify SEO, paid
Activation covers unboxing, setup, first session, paywall
Retention covers lifecycle, community
Referral covers gifting, reviews
Revenue covers blended LTV with hardware + subscription + accessories
Recognizes Series A tier in budget recommendations
Idea bank skips ideas that conflict with brand fit, with explicit rationale

evals.prompt: Just give me a quick marketing plan. Don't make it long.
evals.expected_output: Should resist defaulting to a short plan. Should explain that a marketing-plan is the comprehensive fCMO-deliverable artifact (~10K words) and that for a single-channel quick plan, the channel-specific skill is the right tool (emails, ads, seo-audit, etc.). Should offer alternatives: (a) full marketing-plan as designed, or (b) point to a specific skill for the user's actual need. Should NOT silently produce a stripped-down 3K-word plan that misses the ops stack or the idea bank.
assertions: Resists short-plan request and explains why
Names marketing-plan as the comprehensive fCMO artifact
Recommends channel-specific skills for single-channel quick plans
Offers alternatives clearly
Does not silently produce a stripped-down plan

evals.prompt: A founder wants a plan but keeps asking 'what's the one channel that will make us blow up?' They also want a defensible way to split the budget so they don't starve future growth, and a way to know when a channel is running out of steam. Frame the strategic thinking for the plan.
evals.expected_output: Should push back on silver-bullet thinking with the marketing-as-investing framing — a compounding portfolio, 'no silver bullets, a hundred golden pellets,' one asset that ranks + earns backlinks + feeds the newsletter + becomes a talk, audition not an auction, hope is not a strategy. Should apply the problem size x frequency market-quality gate to sanity-check whether the product is even in a build-big-and-frequent quadrant. Should introduce the 70/20/10 resource-allocation rule (current / next / experimental) so future growth stays funded. Should introduce a weekly tracking cadence with plateau-indicator alerts (flattening week-over-week additions, rising CAC, effort up / output flat) that trigger shifting weight to the next S-curve. Should tie these into Section 2 (Strategic frame), Section 10 (12-month outlook), and Section 13 (Measurement).
assertions: Rejects silver-bullet framing using marketing-as-investing / compounding portfolio
Uses the 'no silver bullets, a hundred golden pellets' and 'audition, not an auction' framing
Invokes 'hope is not a strategy' — every move has a mechanism and leading indicator
Applies the problem size x frequency market-quality gate
Introduces the 70/20/10 resource-allocation rule (current / next / experimental)
Introduces a weekly tracking cadence with plateau-indicator alerts
Ties plateau alerts to shifting weight toward the next S-curve
Maps the framing to Section 2, Section 10, and Section 13

evals.prompt: Before we build the plan, how big is the market for an AI call-summary tool for sales teams at mid-size B2B SaaS companies? The founder keeps quoting a '$12B AI productivity market' to investors.
evals.expected_output: Should define the market boundary in one sentence (geography, buyer, use case, price model) before estimating. Should push back on the single top-down $12B figure as TAM that proves nothing about demand. Should use references/market-sizing.md to separate TAM, SAM, and SOM in plain terms, with SOM as the number that matters for the plan. Should triangulate across at least two of the four methods (bottom-up, search-led, competitor-led, channel-led), show the math for each, and compare results, explaining any gap larger than ~3x. Should present ranges with assumptions listed separately from observed facts, never a single precise number without sources. Should label each estimate high / medium / low / unknown confidence and name the assumption that would most change the answer plus how to test it. May score the 10-factor attractiveness scorecard and tie the SOM range into Section 2, Section 10, and Section 13 open decisions.
assertions: Defines the market boundary before sizing
Challenges the single top-down $12B figure rather than adopting it
Distinguishes TAM, SAM, and SOM and treats SOM as the planning number
Triangulates across at least two sizing methods with visible math
Presents ranges with stated assumptions, not a single precise number
Labels each estimate with a confidence level
Names the highest-impact assumption and a way to validate it

evals.prompt: We start at $1M ARR and target $2M year-end ARR. Monthly ARPC is $50, CAC $100. Assume existing-base revenue retention 85% with no expansion, and new acquisitions retain 85% of their ARR by year end. A colleague budgets $196,118 using only the $1M net increase divided by retention. Is that enough? Show a reconciled year-end ARR bridge and round customers up.
evals.expected_output: Should first retain $850K of starting ARR, leaving $1.15M retained new-customer ARR needed. Each acquired customer contributes $50*12*.85=$510 at year end, requiring ceil(1150000/510)=2255 customers and $225500 before buffer. Reconcile $850000+2255*$510=$2000050. Explain omitted $150K starting-base churn in the old approach. Treat the new-cohort retention as the supplied assumption, not a universal full-year retention multiplier; revenue and logo retention differ.
assertions: Retains the starting base before computing the acquisition gap
Replaces existing-base losses as well as delivering net growth
Uses 2255 customers and $225500 before optional buffer
Reconciles ending ARR to $2000050
States acquisition timing and revenue-retention assumptions

evals.prompt: Build a 12-month marketing plan for [ABC]. They're a home-services client — the account lead wants it for the next monthly session. The owner also keeps asking how big their market is.
evals.expected_output: Should detect BML client work and check .agents/product-marketing.md for 'Generated for [ABC]' (run product-marketing Load if missing or for another client), then read the rules file. Should apply the scope gate: confirm page 00 has at least one Active service (any Active service authorizes a plan) before drafting. Should read page 13 and the Monthly Context Brief before asking anything, and ask only about gap rows by ID (e.g. B-10, I-4), never about funding, burn or investors. Should frame AARRR as found → lead → booked → repeat/referral → signed job, size the plan to B-10 budget, I-8 team time and B-6/I-10 capacity and seasonality, and use Windsor.ai and Semrush (read-only) rather than Ahrefs/Stripe/GA4 MCPs. Every client fact cites a row; missing facts become [NEEDS PROOF: <row>]. Each move shows its retainer status. Written in Baker house style, not the client's voice, ending with the context footer with 'Distinctiveness: n/a for agency artifacts'. Should not write to ~/marketing-plans, Notion or GitHub; saves to the session outputs folder and offers to save to the client's Drive strategy folder and a ClickUp strategy task only on approval. For the market-size question, should not produce TAM/SAM/SOM or a market dollar figure: should answer from the local-market rows (L-1 market definition, L-2 demographics, L-3 local search demand, L-4–L-7 competitors and CPCs) with their sources and dates, recommend bml/local-market-research.md (via client-context-miner Backfill) if those rows are OPEN or stale, and keep any derived estimate as a range with stated, cited inputs or [NEEDS PROOF: <row>].
assertions: Checks the staged context file belongs to [ABC] and reads the rules file
Applies the page 00 scope gate (any Active service) before drafting
Reads page 13 and the Monthly Context Brief before asking; asks only about gap rows by ID
Does not ask about funding rounds, burn, runway or investors
Maps AARRR to a local-service funnel (lead → booked → signed job)
Sizes moves to B-10 budget, I-8 team time and B-6/I-10 capacity and seasonality
Uses Windsor.ai and Semrush read-only, not Ahrefs/Stripe/GA4 MCPs
Cites row IDs for client facts and uses [NEEDS PROOF: <row>] for missing ones
Ends with the context footer showing Distinctiveness n/a
Does not save to ~/marketing-plans, Notion or GitHub; Drive/ClickUp writes only on approval
Answers market size from L rows (L-1–L-3, L-4–L-7) rather than TAM/SAM/SOM, routing OPEN or stale L rows to local-market-research, with no invented market figure

evals.prompt: /marketing-plan [ABC] — pick up where we left off on their plan
evals.expected_output: Should not look for ~/marketing-plans/abc/progress.md. Should find the client's ClickUp task tagged 'strategy' named 'Marketing Plan — [ABC] — v<N>' via the router or a filtered query of the client's Master Task List (no workspace-wide search), read the progress block in its description, and fetch the working file from Drive by the ID listed there (no Drive browsing). Should resume at the next unapproved section. If the phase is 'finalized', should ask whether to revise as v<N+1>, start a new plan, or re-open a section. If no task exists, should say so and offer to start fresh rather than guessing. Should not update the task or Drive file without the user's approval.
assertions: Does not read or create ~/marketing-plans paths
Locates the ClickUp strategy task by router or filtered task query, not broad search
Fetches the working file by Drive ID rather than browsing Drive
Resumes from the next unapproved section
Asks before revising a finalized plan
Does not write to ClickUp or Drive without approval

evals.prompt: Draft the marketing plan for [XYZ], a multi-location dental group. Lean into urgency offers like 'only 5 new-patient slots left this month', and show what unlocks when they raise their next round. Half the budget answers I'm giving you now: they spend about <n> a month, split across Google Ads and print.
evals.expected_output: Should apply both the clinical and multi-location segment rules. Should decline scarcity/urgency framing for a clinical client unless a page 12 row permits it, naming the rule, and offer reassurance-based alternatives (access, process clarity, credentials, approved social proof). Should replace funding-round unlocks with budget, capacity, season and tracking triggers. Should treat the budget answer as a DRAFT row (B-10), flag it in the plan, stage it in the review format and not write it to ClickUp. Should keep each location's proof, hours and providers separate. Because sections rest on a DRAFT row, should mark the plan 'Internal draft — not for client' and not move it to client review. Should flag tracking pixels and lead forms on patient pages for a person instead of recommending them.
assertions: Blocks or drops urgency/scarcity framing for the clinical client and names the rule
Offers reassurance-based alternatives
Replaces funding-round unlocks with budget/capacity/season triggers
Treats the in-session budget answer as DRAFT (B-10), flags it and stages it for review without writing to ClickUp
Keeps location-specific proof, hours and providers separate
Marks the plan internal-only while any section rests on a DRAFT row
Flags pixels/forms on patient pages for human review instead of adding them

evals.prompt: Make a full marketing plan for [DEF] including a paid ads program. Their page 00 shows 'SEO — Active' and 'Strategy — Active — planning only'; no paid media line.
evals.expected_output: Should pass the scope gate because page 00 has an Active service (any Active service authorizes a plan), noting the 'planning only' qualifier means BML plans but doesn't own execution. Should include paid moves only as 'No — scope note' items: owner client or TBD, never BML, listed together in Section 13 as internal upsell opportunities for the account lead (move, the BML service that would cover it, supporting rows), removed before the plan reaches the client. Should mark SEO moves 'Yes' and assign BML roles as owners. Should not invent paid budgets or CPLs; uses A-9/L-7 rows or [NEEDS PROOF]. Section 12 should take fit tags and local versions from marketing-ideas' bml-local-service-fit.md, list applicable ideas by their existing numbers plus relevant BML-<n> local plays, and give a skip list grouped by reason (e.g. SaaS-only, not recommended) rather than one row per skipped idea.
assertions: Passes the scope gate on an Active page 00 service and explains the 'planning only' qualifier
Marks paid moves 'No — scope note' with a non-BML owner
Lists out-of-scope moves together in Section 13 as internal upsell opportunities for the account lead, stripped before client delivery
Does not invent paid budgets or CPLs
Uses existing marketing-ideas numbers and BML-<n> plays with tags from the marketing-ideas fit file, plus a grouped skip list
